subject.value: two luminous foreground relationship medallions for Lesson 2A major third (left) versus minor third (right)

visual_structure.value: Exactly two separate wide oval medallions side by side on pure white, with a slim glowing glass bridge joining them at mid-height. Each medallion is a thin-walled translucent glass-and-watercolor halo: a delicate luminous ring of layered translucent glass, a few fine concentric halo rings just outside it, and tasteful filigree edging hugging the ring (not spreading into the white). The LEFT medallion is a little wider and tinted antique amber (#AB812D); the RIGHT is a little narrower and tinted orchid violet (#8964A4). Each medallion's interior is a large, quiet, near-white milky glass clearing (about 75% of its area) with no texture, no ornament and no dark colour, reserved for exact native keyboard drawings and text. Medallions sit in the middle band of the canvas: roughly the vertical span 20% to 85% of the height, each about 44% of the width, with at least 6% pure white margin on all four canvas sides. Above and below the medallions the canvas is empty pure white.

accent_identity.value: left medallion antique amber #AB812D, right medallion orchid violet #8964A4; identifies the two interval relationships only

negative_space.value: everything outside the two medallions and the bridge is empty pure white (#FFFFFF): no wash, no mist, no glow field, no swirl, no texture, no paper grain, no vignette

background.value: pure flat white (#FFFFFF) isolation for alpha extraction; objects have soft organic translucent edges that fade cleanly to white; nothing touches the canvas edge; no ground, no shadow on the ground, no rectangle
